extracted.intended_audience: Title IX Coordinators, institutional legal counsel/compliance officers at LEAs, IHEs, and other recipients of Department of Education funds; policy analysts and administrators implementing the Title IX final rule
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory Impact Analysis and implementation guidance accompanying the Department of Education's Title IX final rule, describing recipient obligations (e.g., supportive measures, grievance-procedure revisions, training, notice requirements), modeling assumptions, and estimated burdens and costs for LEAs, IHEs, and other federal fund recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer and coordinate supportive measures upon notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(f)(1)(ii) and (g): upon being notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX, including sex-based harassment and prohibited retaliation, a Title IX Coordinator must offer and coordinate supportive measures, as appropriate, to the complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(g) clarifies that for allegations of sex discrimination other than sex-based harassment or retaliation, providing supportive measures does not require the recipient (or its employees/agents) to alter the alleged discriminatory conduct for the purpose of providing a supportive measure. The final requirement covers prohibited retaliation and other forms of sex discrimination; the Department expects the number of incidents in which parties will seek supportive measures to increase compared to the 2020 amendments, and includes related costs in its model. For sex-based harassment and retaliation, types of supportive measures are generally similar and modeled together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective steps to prevent continuation/recurrence (hostile-environment standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require a recipient to take prompt and effective steps to ensure that sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment that creates a hostile environment based on sex, does not continue or recur in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This hostile-environment standard encompasses conduct addressed in enforcement practice prior to the 2020 amendments and is the baseline obligation for recipient response under the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of additional bases of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations explicitly cover sex discrimination based on sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes inclusion of these bases may result in a 10 percent increase in the number of investigations conducted annually because some recipients may not have fully addressed such incidents absent a specific regulatory requirement. This inclusion informed modeling of increased investigations and associated costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow complaints from persons who are not students or employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.45(a)(2) permits a person other than a student or employee who is participating or attempting to participate in a recipient's education program or activity to make a complaint of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes this change will result in a minimal increase in a recipient's overall number of complaints because such complaints are somewhat uncommon, but they can inform recipients of some incidents. Handling of non-student/non-employee complaints will vary by recipient type and process used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient behavior model: Groups A, B, and C
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 2020 amendments, the Department models recipients as falling into one of three groups regarding how they handled complaints that fell outside §106.45: Group A (did not adopt a new process); Group B (handled through a different grievance process/alternative disciplinary process); Group C (handled through a process similar to the §106.45 grievance process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department applies assumed distributions (e.g., ~5% of LEAs and IHEs in Group A, ~90% of LEAs and 50% of IHEs in Group B, etc.) to estimate changes in number of investigations and burden. Expected effects differ by group: Group A recipients likely will revise grievance procedures and see greater per-incident burden reductions due to flexible procedures; Group B will see increases but smaller than Group A; Group C is expected to see little change in number of investigations but may need procedural/recordkeeping revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to revise grievance procedures to comply with final §§106.45/106.46
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department assumes all recipients will need to revise their grievance procedures based on the final regulations, including IHEs' need to comply with final §106.46 as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated one-time revision burden per recipient: 12 hours for a Title IX Coordinator, 2 hours for an administrator, and 6 hours for a lawyer. Total one-time cost estimated at $55,183,830 across recipients. Revisions include adapting procedures to be prompt, equitable, and tailored to the recipient's context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to read and understand the final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: All recipients must spend time reading and understanding the final regulations to determine necessary policy and practice changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department estimates on average 4 hours each for a Title IX Coordinator ($96.46/hour) and a lawyer ($146.58/hour) per recipient to complete this task, yielding a one-time Year 1 cost estimate (presented as ~$24,058,044 across recipients). Some recipients may rely on third‑party summaries which could reduce burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and updating notice of nondiscrimination statements (§106.8(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must post nondiscrimination statements on their websites consistent with final §106.8(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department estimates that ~40% of LEAs, ~20% of IHEs, and ~50% of other institutions will experience more than de minimis burden to modify existing statements. For recipients that have not completed the requirement, assumed effort is 1 hour from the Title IX Coordinator and 2 hours from a web developer; total one-time cost estimated at $2,032,842.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements: timing, content, and Title IX Coordinator training
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require all employees to be trained promptly upon hiring or a change of position that alters their Title IX duties and annually thereafter on the scope of conduct constituting sex discrimination (including definition of 'sex-based harassment') and notification requirements under §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44. Training also must be provided to Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and others with implementation authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes overall annual burden for most employees will not materially increase, but Title IX Coordinators will require more extensive training (assumed 2 hours longer in Year 1 and 1 hour longer in future years). Estimated Year 1 costs for Title IX Coordinator training and development are provided (e.g., $4,774,191 Year 1 training cost; $2,387,096 subsequent years), and updating training materials is also estimated ($9,548,382 one-time assumed for Title IX Coordinator materials development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures are distinct from remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: For allegations of sex discrimination other than sex-based harassment or prohibited retaliation, the recipient's provision of supportive measures does not require the recipient to alter the alleged discriminatory conduct; eliminating the source of sex discrimination is not required as a supportive measure and may only be provided as a remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many instances (e.g., unequal access to facilities) have few appropriate supportive measures besides eliminating the discriminatory source (a remedy). For educational-setting discrimination (e.g., different treatment by a teaching assistant), appropriate supportive measures are likely academic in nature and of relatively minor cost (e.g., switching sections, counseling). The Department used common supportive measures in cost estimates because the variety makes full-spectrum costing impracticable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling assumptions for cost estimates (wages, loading factor, recipients counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's cost model uses median hourly wages for personnel employed in the education sector (BLS data) and a loading factor of 2.0 to account for employer compensation and indirect costs; results are presented rounded in text but use unrounded values in calculations. Recipient counts used: 17,916 LEAs, 6,003 IHEs, and 828 other recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes wide variation among recipients (size, administrative structure) and states the estimates reflect average burdens; estimates may under- or over-state burdens for particular entities. The model also incorporates prior RIA estimates and stakeholder feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated increase in use of grievance procedures and investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department expects that the final regulations will increase use of recipients' grievance procedures by students and others, resulting in an increase in prompt and equitable resolution of complaints and has estimated a 10 percent increase in investigations annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 10 percent figure is used in the Department's cost modeling to estimate potential reductions in prevalence and adverse effects of sex discrimination and to calculate net cost (the RIA cites an estimated net cost of $4,636,200). The Department acknowledges uncertainty due to lack of comprehensive post-2020 data and reliance on anecdotal information.
